_: The part-authoring loop, served by mcp-toolkit's loop kit (docs-release/LOOPS.md) instead of by
tools/mcp/server.mjs. Everything that proxy did EXCEPT its nine armorpieces_* tools is here: the
keep-list over Blockbench's manifest, the description NOTES, the instructions paragraph, and the
check after every editing call. The nine stay in the proxy, which runs under
ARMORPIECES_BB_PROFILE=kit so the two servers do not both offer place_cube.
REWRITTEN 2026-09-07 FOR THE TOOLKIT'S OWN BLOCKBENCH PLUGIN (toolkit 0.133.0+,
mcptoolkit_bridge.js on 127.0.0.1:25801; BLOCKBENCH_BRIDGE_DESIGN.md). The third-party plugin's
94 tools became 26, so most of the old keep-list named things that no longer exist:
remove/rename/duplicate_element -> `element`; the eight painting tools and activate_texture ->
`texture`; save_checkpoint -> `project op:save`. 29 kept names became 18, and three of the traps
below are DEAD - see 'What the new plugin fixed'.
ONE DIFFERENCE from the proxy, stated: it ran check_part.py against the piece's DIRECTORY, read
from a meta.json the Armor Pieces plugin writes on every edit, and only when that file's `seq`
had moved. A `run` here has no meta.json, so `run` points at tools/check_active.py, which does
that lookup. The mechanism gate replaces the seq check: an editing tool ran, so the piece may
have changed, so the check runs - one time too many rather than one too few. The gate now reads
the plugin's OWN stamp (every manifest entry carries `mechanism`, and a mixed tool stamps each
reply), so the old `not` list naming capture_screenshot and set_camera_angle is gone: both
declare themselves `observe` and were never selected by it.
THE KEEP-LIST IS PRICED. Every name here is paid on EVERY turn of every session in this
workspace, and a part session is 40+ turns. The toolkit's `art` base keeps 25 of the plugin's 26;
this keeps 18. What `art` has that a part author does not need: `project` (armorpieces_open /
_save / _close own the tab, and letting a session save or close it behind their back is how a
piece is lost - the proxy also BINDS this session to the piece on open, so the plugin refuses
another session's edit to it), `create_texture` and `apply_texture` (the plugin makes a piece's
sheets; armorpieces_set_part makes the mask sheets), `export_model` (armorpieces_save writes the
geometry), `animation` (nothing in a piece moves), `trigger_action` (drives the app's menus
blind), `paint_faces` and `paint_ascii` - see below.
paint_faces / paint_ascii stay out for the reason they always did, now that they are the
plugin's own rather than the shim's: on the master sheet a value is a position on the trim
material's RAMP, so a colour has to be folded to its luminance, and only armorpieces_paint does
that. A generic painter would write colour onto a greyscale sheet and the check would then
report it.
WHAT THE NEW PLUGIN FIXED, so these notes no longer carry them (each verified live on this
workspace's Blockbench, 2026-09-07):
- Renaming a BONE. `rename_element` used to die inside Blockbench's undo snapshot on a group,
so a mis-named bone meant re-placing its cubes. `element op:rename` keeps groups out of the
snapshot's element list and renames them; `element op:reparent` moves them.
- The GHOST CUBE. Undoing a place_cube left the cube behind outside every group. The plugin
hands its created things to the undo entry now, so an undo removes them.
- CLEARING PAINT. Erasing by drawing at opacity 0 left the sheet untouched, so armorpieces_paint
with `value: null` was the only thing that wrote. `texture op:rects` with `c: null` clears,
and reports how many texels it cleared.
STILL TRUE, and the reason the notes below are worth their per-turn cost: REWORKS LEAVE STRAYS.
Every remove / modify_cube / re-place re-lays the sheet, and paint from the PREVIOUS layout
survives wherever no new face landed on it. The check counts those pixels but does not say where
they are. What is new is a cheap way to find them: `inspect faces` prints the CURRENT face
rectangles, so the stray pixels are what is painted outside them - which is why `inspect` is in
the keep-list and its predecessor was not.
RE-CUT 2026-09-08 ON EVIDENCE, not on judgement. The four Dragonslayer runs of that evening
(docs/measurements/CONCURRENCY_AB.md round 2) were counted against what each tool costs per turn,
and ELEVEN of the nineteen served names were never called once: texture, get_texture, risky_eval,
tool_surface, set_camera_angle, find_elements_by_criteria, undo, redo, get_undo_stack,
list_textures, get_selection - about 2.5k tok of prefix on every turn, 49% of this manifest.
Four came out, and only four, because the sample is four pieces that needed no rework:
- set_camera_angle  capture_screenshot {views} composes a contact sheet; measured 2.7 calls
per piece on the old plugin, ~0 on this one, and 0 here. Superseded.
- find_elements_by_criteria, get_selection   never called in any era; list_outline and the
edit replies already carry what they return.
- redo              undo is the escape from a mistake; redoing one has never been wanted.
What stayed unused and stayed anyway, so the next reader does not 'finish the job': texture,
get_texture and inspect are the REWORK tools - a re-laid sheet leaves stray paint and these are
how it is found - and none of the four pieces reworked. undo and get_undo_stack are the same
insurance. risky_eval is the escape hatch AND the health metric: it is 0.0 in every clean run of
every era, and 11.5 in the contended C-era runs, so its count is how a loss of trust in the tools
shows up in the numbers. Removing it would hide that. tool_surface is the shim's own and is not
reachable from this list.
The honest size of this: 534 tok/turn, about 10% of the manifest and roughly a third of a cent a
piece. The real lever measured that evening was not the manifest at all - it was what a session
READS. One sibling brief was 48% of everything a session carried, which is what
docs/plans/briefs/LESSONS.md now replaces. The next real cut is mid-session phases
(mcp-toolkit TODO.md 1.7): nothing in the painting half calls place_cube, add_group or element.

notes.place_cube: In an Armor Piece: put the cubes in a bone group under `part` (`group`), in Blockbench space (feet at y=0, +Y up; the head is y 24..32). Leave `faces` and `texture` alone - the plugin gives every part cube box UV in free space on the sheet and grows the sheet when full. Cubes do not rotate in this format; rotate the bone group instead. The reply's face rectangles are what to paint next, so place a bone's cubes in ONE call.
notes.modify_cube: In an Armor Piece leave `uv_offset`, `autouv` and `rotation` alone: box UV is laid out by the plugin on every resize (paint moves with the faces), and a rotated cube is a rotated bone group. `inflate` is fine. A resize RE-LAYS the sheet: paint from the old layout survives wherever no new face landed on it, which the check counts as stray pixels - `inspect faces` gives the new rectangles to subtract.
notes.add_group: In an Armor Piece a group under `part` is a bone: its `origin` is the pivot the game rotates about and `rotation` is the only rotation this format has. `parent` names the bone above it, or `part`. Never rotate the `part` group itself - bb_geo reads only the bones inside it, so the yaw would be lost on save; bake it onto the anchor bone.
notes.element: In an Armor Piece: `rename` and `reparent` work on a bone as well as a cube (the old plugin could not rename a group), and `set {origin, rotation}` re-aims one after the fact - so build a bone straight, look at it, then rotate it, rather than precomputing angles. MOVING A BONE'S `origin` MOVES ONLY ITS PIVOT, never the cubes inside it: to reposition a limb, change the bone origins AND every cube's from/to by the same delta in one pass. `remove` on a bone takes its cubes with it. Do not remove or reparent anything under the locked `reference` group - that is the player wearing real armor.
notes.inspect: In an Armor Piece: `faces` is the cheapest way to get every current face rectangle, which is what stray paint is measured against after a rework; `envelope` gives the neighbours on this bone (armorpieces_open already prints them once). Clearance past the body and the armor shells is the piece's own check, not this.
notes.get_texture: An Armor Piece's sheets are `part`, `part_static` and `part_<fitting>`; `preview` is the material preview, read-only. TWO NAMES FOR ONE SHEET, and this costs a turn every time: armorpieces_paint takes the SHEET ID (`part`, `part_static`, `part_<fitting>`), but this tool resolves the texture by the name BLOCKBENCH holds, which for everything except the master is the FILE name (`<piece>_static.png`, `<piece>_<fitting>.png`) - `part_guard` comes back "no texture". `list_textures` prints the names this tool wants. The picture comes back too small to read a 64x32 sheet - use `texture op:read`, or trust the check.
notes.texture: Sheets of an Armor Piece are `part` (the master; greyscale, its value is a position on the trim material's ramp), `part_static` (real colour) and `part_<fitting>` (one greyscale mask per masked fitting). TWO NAMES FOR ONE SHEET, and this costs a turn every time: armorpieces_paint takes the SHEET ID (`part`, `part_static`, `part_<fitting>`), but this tool resolves the texture by the name BLOCKBENCH holds, which for everything except the master is the FILE name (`<piece>_static.png`, `<piece>_<fitting>.png`) - `part_guard` comes back "no texture". `list_textures` prints the names this tool wants. `op:read` prints the texels as characters, which is how to see what is actually on the sheet. `op:rects` with `c: null` CLEARS, and says how many texels it cleared - that is how stray paint from an old layout goes away. For whole faces use armorpieces_paint instead: it folds a colour to the master's ramp, shades a [top, bottom] pair row by row, and takes every face in one call. Do not `op:resize` or `op:remove` a piece's sheet; the plugin owns their size.
notes.capture_screenshot: Looking at an Armor Piece: `fit` frames the model, `views` composes several presets into one contact sheet - one call rather than an angle and a capture each. It is legibility only; geometry comes from the check.
notes.undo: In an Armor Piece one undo step is one edit including the UV layout and paint moves it caused, so undoing a resize also undoes the repaint that followed it in the same entry. Read `get_undo_stack` before undoing more than one.
notes.risky_eval: Every eval is one undo entry unless it changed nothing. `armorpieces_api` is the Armor Pieces plugin's scripting surface, but prefer the armorpieces_* tools: they know the traps. Never close or switch projects inside an eval - use armorpieces_open and armorpieces_close, which also bind this session to the piece.

profile.instructions: Blockbench is running with the Armor Pieces plugin. Open your piece with armorpieces_open (or armorpieces_new) before anything else: that binds this session to it, so every call here goes to that piece by name and another session's edit to it is refused. The locked `reference` group is the player wearing real armor; never edit it. Model inside the `part` group, every cube in a bone group under it, in Blockbench coordinates (feet at y=0, +Y up). Cubes do not rotate; rotate the bone group. Box UV is automatic - never set UV offsets. Every reply to an editing call ends with the piece's check: fix what it names before moving on, and armorpieces_save refuses while problems stand unless you force it with a reason.
